claims.summary: Over F_p, for a degree-D pseudoideal containing the Boolean axioms, families (g_mu,i) of degree<=d with approximators P_mu of degree<=a, kernels Z_mu(k), joint kernel Z(k), joint rank phi(k), W_nu(k) the joint kernel of the other families and marginal m_nu(k)=dim W_nu(k)-dim Z(k), with K>=d and a+K+pd<=D: phi(k)/N_n(k) is nonincreasing (Pang's Lemma 4.1 for intersections); some q in family nu's span makes P_nu(1-q^(p-1)) enlarge the joint kernel by at least (1-1/p)m_nu(K-d) (Pang's Lemma 4.2 on the subspace W_nu(K-d)), and every refinement of family nu alone by at most m_nu(K). All marginals can vanish with full joint rank (F_2, the degree-3 vanishing ideal of {0,1}^2, K=d=1, families {1+y},{x+y},{y}, phi=3), so refining one family at a time has no per-step contraction of the joint rank. One simultaneous round can gain nothing too: F_2, the degree-4 vanishing ideal of {0,1}^4, K=d=1, P=1, the six pair families {x_i,x_j}: every choice of q_ij leaves the joint kernel 0 (Sauer-Shelah), with phi(1)=5 and phi(0)=1.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with a follow-up; part (d), the zero-gain round, is the reviewer's counterexample, proved in the entry and checked in the follow-up.
claims.rationale: Bounds the step of any one-family-at-a-time joint version of Pang's recurrence, after the source showed his approximators are not linear in the input.
claims.next_action: Simultaneous refinement of all families in one round.
